title: Homology Modeling, Screening, and Identification of Potential FOXO6 Inhibitors Curtail Gastric Cancer Progression: an In Silico Drug Repurposing Approach.
authors: Poleboyina, Sneha Malleswari; Poleboyina, Pavan Kumar; Pawar, Smita C; Guntuku, Girijasankar
one_liner_zh: 该文通过同源建模和分子对接筛选FOXO6转录因子抑制剂以治疗胃癌，虽涉及TF-DNA互作对象但未研究结合机制，方法仅用对接无AI/物理模拟深度，属广义蛋白-配体药物筛选，对本课题启发有限。
abstract: Gastric cancer is the world's second leading cause of cancer-related fatalities, with the epidemiology changing over the previous several decades. FOXOs are the O subfamily of the forkhead box (FOX) transcription factor family, which consists of four members: FOXO1, FOXO3, FOXO4, and FOXO6. FOXO6 mRNA and protein levels are increased in gastric cancer tissues. FOXO6 forced overexpression enhances gastric cancer cell growth, while knockdown decreases proliferation. In our study, the GEPIA, Kaplan-Meier, KEGG, and STRING databases were used to determine FOXO6 mRNA expression, overall survival ratio, interactive pathways, and top 10 associated proteins in gastric cancer respectively. Due to the lack of a solved structure for FOXO6, homology modeling was performed to obtain a 3D structure model, and we used anti-cancer drugs and small molecules to target FOXO6 for identifying a potential selective FOXO6 inhibitor. The chemical composition of the proteins and ligands has a significant impact on docking procedure performance. With this in mind, a critical evaluation of the performance of three regularly used docking routines was carried out: MVD, AutoDock Vina in PyRx, and ArgusLab. The binding affinities, docking scores, and intermolecular interactions were used as assessment criteria. In the study, the porfimer sodium showed excellent binding affinity to the FOXO6 protein. The major three docking software packages were used to analyze the scoring/H-bonding energy and intermolecular interactions. Based on the results, we concluded that FOXO6 was upregulated in gastric cancer and the ligand porfimer sodium emerges as a promising potential FOXO6 inhibitor to curtail gastric cancer progression.
abstract_zh: 胃癌是全球癌症相关死亡的第二大原因，其流行病学在过去几十年中发生了变化。FOXOs是叉头框（FOX）转录因子家族的O亚家族，包含四个成员：FOXO1、FOXO3、FOXO4和FOXO6。在胃癌组织中，FOXO6的mRNA和蛋白水平升高。FOXO6的强制过表达促进胃癌细胞生长，而其敲低则减少增殖。在本研究中，我们分别使用GEPIA、Kaplan-Meier、KEGG和STRING数据库来确定胃癌中FOXO6的mRNA表达、总生存率、交互通路及前10个相关蛋白。由于缺乏FOXO6的已解析结构，我们进行了同源建模以获得三维结构模型，并使用抗癌药物和小分子靶向FOXO6，以识别潜在的选择性FOXO6抑制剂。蛋白质和配体的化学组成对对接程序的性能有显著影响。鉴于此，我们对三种常用对接程序（MVD、PyRx中的AutoDock Vina和ArgusLab）的性能进行了关键评估。结合亲和力、对接分数和分子间相互作用被用作评估标准。研究中，卟吩姆钠（porfimer sodium）显示出对FOXO6蛋白优异的结合亲和力。使用这三种主要对接软件包分析了评分/氢键能量和分子间相互作用。基于结果，我们得出结论：FOXO6在胃癌中上调，配体卟吩姆钠有望成为抑制胃癌进展的潜在选择性FOXO6抑制剂。
